notes.title: The Qualities of a Protégé
notes.summary: Dr. Angel taught the 10 qualities of a protege, from being a master listener to honoring your mentor, with the ping pong coach illustration on strengthening strengths instead of fixing weaknesses. A bonus teaching covered liars, truth, and accuracy: how to tell deliberate deceivers from people who are simply inaccurate, and why accuracy has its place. The class also named guilt and shame as what keeps a protege from approaching a mentor, and pointed ahead to the next teaching, Discovering the Power of Purpose.
notes.full_text:
# NCU Class Notes — Thursday, October 29, 2026
Teacher: Dr. Angel. Topic: The Qualities of a Protégé.
(Summarized from the class transcript Ralph shared after class. Class ran past 7:26 p.m.; Ms. Lynn took attendance and closed in prayer.)

## The 10 qualities

1. **Be a master listener.** Total focus on the mentor: no calls, no texting, no reading. Part of listening is writing it down. A short pencil is better than a long memory. Never go before wisdom without pencil and paper.
2. **Learn and discern from an imperfect mentor.** No mentor is perfect in any of their roles. Extract good information from an imperfect source. You will not agree with every book in the program, and that is on purpose.
3. **Clearly define what success means to you.** Success is the fulfillment of a worthy goal. For the believer the heart of it is doing and fulfilling the will of God. Knowing your definition points you to your assignment and, in this context, to the right mentor: find a mentor who has developed success in the direction you want to go.
4. **The protégé pursues and chooses the mentor.** If the mentor chooses the protégé, that is control, not mentorship. The proof of your desire to grow is in your pursuit. The protégé decides how close he gets and how fast he grows. Do not let a mentor seeming out of reach put you off; they are human. A regular voice in your life carries a level of mentorship whether you planned it or not.
5. **Decide what you want to learn.** Set immediate goals: 90 day goals, one to two year goals, long term goals. Goals give focus, and people keep working at what they see growth in. And learn the 11th commandment: blessed are the flexible.
6. **Give your mentor feedback.** It helps the mentor recognize your filter: your thoughts, heart, and motivation. Tell them whether they are helping you or not.
7. **Never regret what you share with your mentor.** It is a personal relationship; unload wrong thoughts and let the mentor correct perspective. The mentor keeps what the protégé shares confidential, but the mentor's teaching may be passed on to others. You cannot move into your tomorrow with yesterday's information.
8. **Everyone has a weakness; a good mentor strengthens strengths.** A mentor concentrates on your strengths and develops them toward genius. A manipulator focuses on your weakness to keep you under. (Illustration: the Chinese ping pong coach, asked about weaknesses: "We ignore their weakness. Strengthen the strengths.")
9. **Be willing to invest in the relationship.** People are like elevators, they take you up or down; invest in the ones who take you up. Relationship costs time and expectation, and honor.
10. **Honor your mentor.** Honor their place in your life. It does not have to be money: sharing their words is honoring, showing up when they teach is honoring, influencing someone else with what they taught you is honoring. That is kingdom.

## Bonus teaching: liars, truth, and accuracy
- Everyone lies in the small sense (saying "I'm fine" when they are not); distinguish deliberate deceivers, who are few and not to be trusted, from people who are simply inaccurate or speaking from their perception.
- Never confront a liar. Take note of what they showed you and move forward; confronting just trains them to deceive better.
- Accuracy is a real gift and the world needs it, but it has its place: essential in a courtroom, less important over coffee with a friend. Not everyone inaccurate is a liar, and not everything accurate is the whole truth; perception shapes reports (50 people, same sunset, 50 descriptions).
- The Bible is the ultimate truth; a doctor's report can be honest and still not be the final word (testimony shared of a friend healed of kidney cancer after prayer and a 40 day fast).

## Also from class
- Guilt and shame will hinder a protégé from choosing and approaching a mentor; dropping them brings discernment.
- Next teaching coming: "Discovering the Power of Purpose," then goal setting. Classes run Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.
- NCU is reviewing and changing curriculum this year.
- Ms. Lynn closed in prayer, including prayer for help with reaction papers, dissertations, and theses.

## Follow-ups involving Ralph
- Dr. Angel asked Ralph about AI help: she is looking forward to seeing some AI canvas and marketing work, asked him to tell her what he wants and send it over, and said they still need to talk and will talk tomorrow (Fri Oct 30). She plans to combine it with other business.
- A classmate asked Ralph to email her the thing he posted on Facebook so she can use it in her dissertation; Ralph said "Feel free to." (Open: the email itself.)
- After class Ralph told the group what Muse did today: cleaned up and unpublished about 500 YouTube videos, scanned his Facebook posts, downloaded the songs, posted them to YouTube with written descriptions, and started the TikTok account the same way.

notes.title: Understanding Purpose (Student Notes)
notes.summary: Fill in the blank student notes for the Understanding Purpose teaching, copyright New Covenant University 2010. It opens with the anchor line My Purpose is My Discovery, on Ecclesiastes 3:1, and works through numbered points on what purpose is and what it requires. Received from Ralph on November 6, 2026, ahead of the Discovering the Power of Purpose teaching. The notes themselves carry no class date or teacher name.
